title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in a Cypress neighborhood, Harris County sheriff's deputies stopped two 19 year old friends, Anthony and Julian, after flock cameras flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. An undercover unit saw a car matching the description, but deputies and a helicopter could not read its plates, so backup was called. At least five patrol cars and a helicopter surrounded Anthony's Camaro. Deputies pointed guns, forced the men to the ground, and handcuffed them. Julian said a deputy threatened to shoot him, and he showed cuts and scrapes. The men were not suspects and faced no charges.

Deputies soon realized they had the wrong car and told the men about the stolen vehicle investigation. Anthony's mother, Leslie, said she plans to hire an attorney and wants deputies held accountable. The sheriff's office said supervisors, including the district captain, shift lieutenants, and shift sergeants, will review body worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed. The men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
